questions.question_text: In typography and poster design, what term describes the adjustment of space between individual pairs of letters to improve visual readability?
When creating a relief sculpture in clay, which technique involves carving away material to leave the subject protruding slightly from the background plane?
In computer graphics, which file format uses mathematical equations to define lines and shapes, ensuring the image can be scaled infinitely without losing quality?
Which printmaking process utilizes a squeegee to force ink through a mesh screen where a stencil has not blocked the pores?
During the armature building phase of a three-dimensional sculpture, what material is primarily used to provide internal structural support?
options: B) Aluminum or galvanized steel wire
questions.answer: B) Aluminum or galvanized steel wire

sections.section_name: Section B - Theory Short Answer Concepts

questions.question_text: Define the structural purpose of an 'armature' in three-dimensional clay sculpting processes. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: An armature acts as the internal skeleton of a sculpture, providing a rigid framework. It supports the weight of wet clay, preventing collapse and maintaining the intended structural proportions during modeling.

questions.question_text: Explain the concept of 'positive and negative space' when designing a stencil for screen printing. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Positive space refers to the open areas of the stencil where ink passes through to create the image. Negative space is the masked, solid area that blocks ink from reaching the substrate.

questions.question_text: Describe the aesthetic function of 'calligraphic flourishes' in formal typography layouts. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Calligraphic flourishes are decorative, sweeping strokes added to letters. They enhance the aesthetic rhythm, fill negative space dynamically, and elevate the visual elegance of formal posters or certificates.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between raster (bitmap) graphics and vector graphics in digital art workflows. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Raster graphics use a grid of colored pixels, losing resolution when enlarged. Vector graphics rely on mathematical paths and polygons, allowing infinite scaling without quality degradation, ideal for logos.

questions.question_text: Outline the fundamental steps to prepare raw terracotta clay for modeling to avoid air bubbles. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Raw clay must undergo 'wedging,' a rigorous kneading process. This aligns clay particles, homogenizes moisture content, and forces out trapped air bubbles that could otherwise cause explosions during kiln firing.

sections.section_name: Section C - Practical Composition & Design Layouts

questions.question_text: Draft practical scoring guidelines for creating a multi-layered stencil print titled 'Urban Landscape'. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Assess the precision of exacto-knife cuts separating three distinct color layers (foreground, midground, background). Scoring depends on perfect registration alignment between layers to prevent color bleeding, clean ink application using a squeegee, and strong contrast in the final architectural composition.

questions.question_text: Formulate a layout matrix for designing an awareness poster on 'Environmental Conservation' combining typography and hand-drawn elements. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The layout must demonstrate a clear visual hierarchy. A bold, sans-serif calligraphic headline should dominate the top third. The central focal point requires a highly saturated, hand-drawn graphic symbol, balanced by smaller, legible body text anchored in the lower margins using the rule of thirds.

questions.question_text: Provide structural guidelines for sculpting a proportional human head in terracotta relief over a flat clay slab. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Begin by establishing the cranial mass and jawline contours. Scoring evaluates the accurate placement of facial features along the central axis: eyes positioned halfway down the skull, nose ending halfway between eyes and chin, ensuring three-dimensional depth projects realistically from the slab base.

sections.section_name: Section D - Applied Art Portfolios & Digital Synthesis

questions.question_text: Detail the curation and digital formatting workflow for assembling an Art Integrated Project Portfolio showcasing a year's worth of mixed-media crafts. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The curation workflow requires photographing physical masks and sculptures under uniform, neutral lighting. These images are imported into desktop publishing software, cropped, and color-corrected. Students must arrange the visual assets chronologically, inserting structured typographic captions detailing materials and concepts, ensuring consistent page margins and a unified cover design for final PDF exportation.

questions.question_text: Explain how a student can utilize digital layering tools in a computer graphics application to transition a scanned pencil sketch into a finalized digital illustration. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The student imports the scanned sketch onto the bottom software layer and lowers its opacity. A new vector layer is created above it to trace crisp, digital outlines. Subsequent layers are added sequentially beneath the line-art for applying flat base colors, blocking in shadows, and adding luminous highlights using digital brush blending modes.
